title: Machine learning and experiments yield tolerant polymer dielectrics
summary: Machine-learning property models and phenomenological screening rules narrowed a list of more than 13,000 previously synthesized polymers to candidates for high-temperature dielectric applications. The authors report experimental testing of selected candidates and derive design rules for electric-field and temperature tolerance. Review is limited to the abstract and publication metadata.
ai_technology: Machine learning and informatics models for polymer dielectric screening
organization: University of Connecticut; Georgia Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: Property-based screening of over 13,000 known polymers, followed by experimental validation of some selected dielectric candidates.
evidence.unknown: Review scope: abstract, online date and affiliations. Candidate-by-candidate property values and the full experimental sample count were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models predicted screening properties such as band gap and cohesive energy density.
